text: You've got a plan for all three layers. Now it's time for the first real code in this pipeline: reading the raw sales extract and landing it, completely untouched, as the Bronze Delta table.

The in-store point-of-sale system drops a daily CSV extract. This reads it with spark dot read, using header and inferSchema options, and writes it straight out as a Delta table in append mode, saved as bronze dot daily sales raw. Notice what's missing on purpose: no dropDuplicates, no type casting, no filtering out anything. Bronze's whole job is to preserve exactly what the source sent.

The online storefront's order events land as JSON instead of CSV, so the reader changes to spark dot read dot json with the multiLine option — but the destination is the same bronze table. The two sources don't match in shape yet, and that's fine. Reconciling them into one common structure is explicitly Silver's job, next lesson, not Bronze's.

Two choices here are worth calling out. First, append mode, not overwrite — every day's run should add on top of every previous day's raw data, because Bronze is the layer you can always go back to if your cleaning logic turns out to be wrong. Second, inferSchema is perfectly fine at this layer, because nothing downstream depends on that guess being exact yet. Starting next lesson, every column that matters gets an explicit, intentional type.
That's the Bronze layer, built. Next lesson, you'll write the transformation that turns this untouched raw data into clean, typed, deduplicated Silver records.
